title: Suspensions, added tones, and extensions
description: Distinguish sus, add, 6, 9/maj9/m9, and alterations — and which symbols imply a 7th.

cards.front: What do sus2 and sus4 mean? Spell Csus2 and Csus4.
cards.back: The 3rd is replaced by the 2nd or 4th. Csus2 = C D G. Csus4 = C F G. Quality is suspended until it resolves or context supplies a third.

cards.front: What is Cadd9, and does it imply a 7th?
cards.back: Triad plus the 9th (2nd): C E G D. No 7th implied.

cards.front: Why is Cadd9 not the same as C9?
cards.back: C9 is a dominant 7 plus 9 (7th implied): C E G Bb D. Cadd9 has no Bb.

cards.front: Spell C6 and Cm6. Which other chord can share C6’s pitch classes?
cards.back: C6 = C E G A. Cm6 = C Eb G A. C6 often = Am7 as a pitch set; bass and context decide the name.

cards.front: Spell C9, Cmaj9, and Cm9. Which 7th does each imply?
cards.back: C9 = C E G Bb D (dominant 7 + 9). Cmaj9 = C E G B D (maj7 + 9). Cm9 = C Eb G Bb D (m7 + 9).

cards.front: What do 11 and 13 add, and what does guitar often omit?
cards.back: Further extensions (11 = 4, 13 = 6). On guitar often omit 5 or even the root. Keep guide tones (3 and 7) when the chord must speak.

cards.front: What are altered tensions, and on which chord type do they usually sit?
cards.back: Chromatic tensions such as b9, #9, #11, b13, usually on dominant. Example: G7b9.

cards.front: How do 9, 11, and 13 relate to 2, 4, and 6?
cards.back: They are the same pitch classes an octave up: 9 = 2, 11 = 4, 13 = 6, usually voiced above the core 3rd/7th.
They delay the third: sus4 to 3, or sus2 to 3.

cards.front: Spell Gsus4, Gadd9, G9, Gmaj9, and G6. Which symbol requires F?
cards.back: Gsus4 = G C D. Gadd9 = G B D A. G9 = G B D F A. Gmaj9 = G B D F# A. G6 = G B D E. G9 requires F (the b7).

cards.front: Why can Am7 and C6 share pitch classes? What decides the name?
cards.back: Both are A C E G / C E G A. Bass and context decide: A in the bass reads as Am7; C in the bass often reads as C6.

cards.front: On 4–3–2, start from C = 10 9 8. How do you hint Csus2 vs Cadd9 vs C9?
cards.back: Csus2: replace E with D. Cadd9: keep E and add D above. C9: imply E + Bb (+ D) over a C bass; compare by including or omitting Bb.

cards.front: Spell G7b9 and how might you play it into C?
cards.back: G B D F Ab. Play a shell plus Ab as a color tone, then resolve into C.

cards.front: Why does reading charts carefully matter for add9 vs 9?
cards.back: Playing a dominant 9 when the writer wanted a plain triad plus 9 adds an unwanted b7.
